newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Last-minute snags hold up Netanyahu-Arafat summit.
newsitem.headline: Last-minute snags hold up Netanyahu-Arafat summit.

text.p: U.S. Middle Envoy Dennis Ross failed on Tuesday to arrange a summit between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to complete a Hebron deal.
"We're still working and I think there is a genuine desire to reach an agreement. So we are going to keep working and I hope we can reach it soon," Ross said after meeting Arafat in Gaza.

Israeli and Palestinian officials had said the two leaders would probably meet on Wednesday as negotiators ironed out most issues but haggling over the release of prisoners and future withdrawals kept the two sides from reaching a deal.
Ross, who has mediated during three months of delicate talks, met Netanyahu before travelling to Gaza for talks with Arafat.
Asked if a summit could take place on Thursday, he told reporters in Gaza: "What I prefer to do is to keep working and we'll see. When we get there, we get there."
Netanyahu's demand for security measures to protect around 400 Jewish settlers in Hebron has held up Israel's redeployement in the West Bank town as outlined in a 1995 Israel-PLO peace deal.
